entries.text:
Pinnock’s English Concert Water Music is still the digital period-instrument classic for these suites: majestic F-major overture, brass that steals the D-major music without blare, G-major dances caught light. Woodwind that often fails on period instruments here holds its place. Against Harnoncourt’s earlier Concentus Musicus tapes it is smoother and studio-clear; against modern-chamber neighbours it restores gut and natural brass as audible stance.

The original Archiv face is Water Music only. Later Fireworks couplings and WM+Fireworks compilations are other objects — do not confuse them with these Henry Wood Hall tapes.

entries.text:
Harnoncourt’s Concentus Musicus Water Music is the pioneering original-instrument statement — swift, brash, ceremonial rather than polished. Horns rasp; dances lean forward; the sense of outdoor occasion is the point. Against Pinnock 1983 it is historically first and deliberately less smooth; keep it for the argument’s opening pole, not as the easiest HIP listen.

Cycle year is 1978 (Telefunken), not a 1990s remake. Standard couplings are organ concertos, not Fireworks. Teldec reissues carry the same Water Music tapes with cleaner transfer options.
